claims.text: Controlled thermal–mechanical pretreatment enhances and stabilizes short-range chemical and structural order in rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys.
Enhanced short-range order promotes a magnetostructural transition.
The promoted magnetostructural transition enhances the magnetocaloric effect at low applied fields.
The proposed treatment can enhance the low-field magnetocaloric effect while preserving rapid heat exchange.
The proposed treatment can enhance the low-field magnetocaloric effect while maintaining low hysteresis.
The proposed treatment can enhance the low-field magnetocaloric effect while preserving mechanical stability.
The as-cast or conventionally processed baseline has a relatively random distribution of atomic configurations and defect structures.
Annealing followed by deformation can tailor local short-range order and defect structures.
Short-range chemical order and engineered defect structures modulate magnetoelastic coupling.
Treatment-induced short-range order creates local magnetostructural heterogeneities.
Local magnetostructural heterogeneities increase magnetoelastic interactions.
Increased magnetoelastic interactions promote a sharp, reversible magnetostructural transition at low applied fields.
A sharp, reversible magnetostructural transition amplifies the magnetic entropy change.
Treated samples will show a larger magnetic entropy change than untreated samples at the same low applied field.
The increase in magnetocaloric response will occur with only a minimal increase in magnetic hysteresis.
The treatment will leave fast heat-exchange properties unchanged.
The hypothesized effect is expected primarily within the temperature window around the magnetic transition and under low applied fields.
The hypothesized effect may be less applicable at extreme temperatures or very high applied fields.
